title: Diagnostic evidence storage
intro: Evidence storage ownership and timing contract. Dark Start here nodes mark graph entry. The sequence diagram begins at its first message. Delivery evidence lives in the diagnostic foundation report.

groups.title: Ownership
groups.description: Keep every blocking evidence call out of the controller.

groups.title: Phases
groups.description: Bound each storage phase without adding to a safety ceiling.

groups.title: Failures
groups.description: Stop forward progress and keep teardown unchanged.

discussion.title: Keep evidence storage off the teardown path
discussion.summary: One separate evidence writer owns the run directory and every blocking file call. The controller sends serialised frames through a bounded outbox and never waits for them, except one bounded intent gate before each acquisition. Command output reaches the controller through pipes. Storage failure stops forward progress and never changes teardown. Publication has its own window, then KILL and a bounded reap.

updatedDiagrams.summary: New view. The writer owns storage. The controller keeps signals, reaps and the outbox.
New view. Readiness, intent gates and publication each have declared bounds.
New view. Each storage failure ends in the in-memory run outcome.

diagrams.title: Give storage to the writer
diagrams.caption: The writer starts no process and sends no signal. The controller records the writer PID from its own spawn call. Commands receive no evidence descriptor, and no child receives a writer pipe end.

diagrams.title: Bound each storage phase
diagrams.caption: Readiness completes before any acquisition. Only intent records wait for an acknowledgement. Publication starts after worker close and ends at P plus two seconds. These bounds never extend the cleanup or disposal ceiling. OS scheduling limits apply.

diagrams.title: Stop forward, keep teardown
diagrams.caption: Storage failure is sticky. The run fails because required evidence is incomplete. The caller receives the outcome in memory, without reading evidence back.
